newsitem.title: USA: Texas could see natural gas shortages this winter.
newsitem.headline: Texas could see natural gas shortages this winter.

text.p: With less natural gas being injected into storage this year compared to last year, Texas could experience shortages this winter, a staff member of the Texas Railroad Commission said on Tuesday.

Nationwide, storage levels appear to be back on track with 1995, but Texas gas storage this year is "not anywhere close to where it was a year ago," said David Schieck, director of head of the commission's oil and gas division.
"There may be some shortages," Schieck said.
Texas producers have not curtailed production, but some made adjustments for over-production earlier this year, contributing to the lagging storage levels, he said.

The commission estimated storage levels in the state rose slightly to 182.8 billion cubic feet (bcf) at September 15. Texas gas in storage in August was 165.1 bcf in August compared to 265.9 bcf in August 1995.
The commission set October production allowables for prorated fields in the state at 2.96 billion cubic feet per day, or 93 percent of actual October 1995 production.
